claim: On a large-scale multilingual LeetCode benchmark, partial-correctness (fractional passed-testcase ratios) is concentrated near the extremes (0% or 100%) rather than spread across intermediate near-miss regions.
stance_target: Competitive/algorithmic-style code evaluation collapses to near-binary outcomes, in contrast to functional/API-composition code where partial pass is common
scope_conditions: 2,707 free LeetCode problems, 12 programming languages, 9 open-weight code LLMs, 325,343 problem-model-language jobs
quoted_support: Wrong-answer cases are concentrated in the zero-percent passed-testcase bin across models, with little evidence of intermediate testcase success... partial correctness is concentrated near the extremes rather than distributed across near-miss regions.

claim: Model rankings on code-generation benchmarks are slice-dependent: the best model by mean correctness is not the best model by hard-problem performance, accepted-problem coverage, or static code quality.
stance_target: Aggregate pass@k obscures multidimensional model differences
quoted_support: Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct is strongest on hard problems and distinct-problem coverage, while Gemma-2-27B-IT achieves the highest all-language lint pass rate.

claim: Compile errors, not wrong answers, are the dominant non-accepted outcome across all 9 evaluated open code LLMs on multilingual LeetCode tasks.
scope_conditions: 9 open code LLMs, 12 languages, LeetCode judge outcomes
quoted_support: compile errors account for 63.25% of non-accepted best submissions, indicating that many failures occur before semantic correctness can be tested.

claim: Functional correctness and static code quality (lint cleanliness, structural regularity) produce different model rankings, showing they measure distinct properties.
stance_target: Multi-metric code evaluation beyond pass rate
scope_conditions: 9 open code LLMs, accepted-code and all-language linter analysis
quoted_support: A model can generate code that is short, regular, and structurally tidy while still failing to compile or solve the task.
